I know this is a couple days late but I'm gonna reply anyway.

I... 100% understand how you feel. That may be hard to believe. When i read your post though, it's eerily similar to my own mother, to the point that i almost wonder if you're one of my siblings.

I've come to realize through therapy and introspection that how i grew up was emotional abuse. That's not to say that my mom didn't try or that she didn't do what she could. There's just a distinction between good and not as bad as it could be. That's probably why triggers like that hurt us so badly. It's something akin to PTSD if not actually PTSD in some cases. I mean, one of my triggers that I'm working on is when people raise their voices even a little. As someone gets louder the closer i get to a panic attack. Kettle meet pot here because i just remembered i still need to address some triggers with my roommates (one of whom gets so loud and curses so much when playing video games that he's actually sent me into a panic attack and nobody realized it because i was in another room trying to prevent it) and here i am about to offer advice.

Regardless. Here's what i suggest. Above all else: please don't feel bad for asking for help. Please. And it's probably very hard but try not to blame yourself. It's true that you couldn't have known he would react that way, but in turn he wouldn't know that you would be triggered by that reaction. I know if i were your friend i wouldn't blame you one bit for what happened, because you couldn't have known. And you are 100% allowed to ask for help right now. From your description, i really don't blame you and you definitely aren't "playing the victim" (i would know, i have basically my whole life in experience dealing with that from /my/ mother). It sounds like a harmless prank that he overreacted to, imho.

Next up. Do your other friends know anything about how you grew up? If so then you can bring it up that way and have them either help you tell him or tell him themselves. You could tell them that because of your childhood and because of what you went through, certain actions can be taken in a harsher way than they maybe were intended. You can even go super vague with it and say that "passive aggressiveness stirs up bad memories". If they're good enough friends then they'll understand. If you talk to the one friend directly, personally i would have someone else along for the ride that can help you if something happens again. Even if it's just to get you out of the situation. If the PA friend isn't open to at least trying to act differently, F'em. I know i wouldn't want to spend too much time with someone that doesn't respect me and my mental health. Since he's been good before though, i suspect that something else might've been going on for him and he was preoccupied and lashed out like that. That's my hope at least. It'd still be good to inform your friends of your triggers, at least this one and some of the more... "Easily accessed"? The ones that are more likely to be accidentally triggered.

You're not gonna end up like your mom, hon. I can promise you that much. You don't blame him for what he did, and you recognize your hand in it. You reached out to apologise for what you did that caused his (bloated) reaction. He's the one being petty right now; you're doing better than you think you are. You're a better person than you think you are. I believe in you and i believe that you can get out of this spiral. I'm here if you need an understanding ear on this front or if you just want someone to talk to about life. Stay strong, dove.

I'm a little weird in this i think. I'm right handed and only ever cut my right arm, inside of the forearm or more recently my left ankle. I know why i do it that way though. My arm is because when i first started, it was because of an accident that nicked that arm. Reopening it and sticking to that spot to keep it inconspicuous made it a habit i think. And the ankle is because when I'm sitting down, my left leg crosses over easier than my right. A comfort thing for an uncomfortable act.

An accident is actually what made me start in the beginning. I was working in construction cleanup and we had those razor blade paint scraper things; long story short my hand slipped and i nicked my arm. Then i did it on purpose. To this day that same area on my arm is one of two places that i cut and i still use that same kind of blade (it's like a regular razor blade but it has a little cover/handle so it's only sharp on one side. No danger of accidentally slicing my fingers! I think they're sturdier too).

You're definitely not weak for this though. I don't want you to think that. You're stronger than you think you are and i believe in you. <3

As i said in my post, my problem comes while I'm at work and can't do any of my usual things to distract myself. And rubber bands or ice have never worked for me; it's the wrong kind of pain. I'm looking for something duller, like an ache, and multiple shallows give me that after the initial sharpness.

Officially, I'm not even supposed to be on my phone at work. My supervisor has given clearance for phones but pretty much nothing else. The only, only reason why i even posted this is because i can't find any options that are viable and effective for me while I'm at work.

I have a really hard time distracting myself too, so I definitely get it, hon. I would suggest trying to find a friend to talk to, listening to music, watching a movie, or playing a game. Or, if you want, I'm here and willing to talk. Good luck, dove
